standard.title: Estimation and rounding
standard.description: Choose and use estimation and rounding to check and explain the reasonableness of calculations including the results of financial transactions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can estimate quantities in collections and assess reasonableness of calculations (AC9M3N05). They have not yet applied rounding systematically to calculations or used estimation in financial contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use rounding and estimation to check the reasonableness of calculations and financial transactions, explaining whether an estimate is above or below the actual answer and why.

nodes.label: Rounding to convenient numbers
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can round numbers to the nearest 10 or 100 and explain the rounding rule.
nodes.minimum_width: Round one number to the nearest 10 and one to the nearest 100; explain the rule for deciding which way to round.
nodes.typical_width: Round two- and three-digit numbers to the nearest 10 or 100; explain the midpoint rule (5 rounds up); apply to prices and measurements; recognise that rounding to a closer power of 10 gives a more accurate estimate.
wider: Investigate rounding in different directions (always up, always down, round-half-up) and discuss when each is appropriate — e.g. always rounding up when budgeting to avoid overspending
Explore how the choice of rounding precision (to nearest 10 vs nearest 100) affects the usefulness of an estimate for different purposes
success_criteria: Students can round any two- or three-digit number to the nearest 10 and 100
Students can explain which way a number rounds and why

nodes.label: Estimation as a check
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use estimation to determine what range a calculation answer should fall within, and identify unreasonable answers.
nodes.minimum_width: Estimate the result of one calculation by rounding and determine a bounding range (the answer will be between ___ and ___); identify whether a given answer is reasonable.
nodes.typical_width: Use rounded estimates to determine a range for calculation results; identify whether computed answers are reasonable; explain the effect of rounding both numbers up, both down, or one each way on the estimate; apply to multi-step calculations.
wider: Investigate the accumulated effect of rounding in multi-step calculations — when does rounding at each step compound into a significant error?
Compare estimation strategies for the same problem: front-end estimation vs rounding vs compatible numbers, and discuss which gives a closer estimate

response_modes.reason: Students need the reasoning scaffold 'what am I over-counting and what am I under-counting when I round?' to develop the habit of predicting estimate direction. Without this, estimation remains a ritual rather than a genuine check on reasonableness.

success_criteria: Students can estimate the result of a calculation and state a bounding range
Students can identify an unreasonable answer using estimation and explain why it is unreasonable

nodes.label: Estimation in financial contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply estimation and rounding to financial transactions and explain their reasoning.
nodes.minimum_width: Estimate the total cost of two or three items by rounding prices; explain whether the estimate is likely to be above or below the actual total.
nodes.typical_width: Use rounded amounts to complete an estimated budget for a shopping trip or event; explain why overestimating is appropriate when budgeting; apply estimation to check financial calculations for reasonableness.
wider: Plan a complete budget for a class event or excursion, using estimation throughout and justifying all rounding decisions in terms of the financial context
Investigate how supermarket price rounding (everything to the nearest 5 cents in cash transactions) is applied and calculate the cumulative effect on a shopping basket
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Financial estimation contexts are authentically motivating and connect to numeracy beyond school. Students who engage with budget estimation develop practical number sense and learn that the direction of rounding is a purposeful choice.
success_criteria: Students can estimate a total cost by rounding prices and explain whether the estimate is an overestimate or underestimate
Students can justify a rounding direction decision in a financial context (e.g. round up to avoid overspending)
